incident-bot: :rotating_light: PROD ALERT — p99 latency spike on continuous-batching path (usw2-gpu). p99 crossed 2.5s for the last 5m (SLO 1.0s). Detecting streaming stalls + elevated queue depth. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.local/alerts/3170001111 :rotating_light:

Sylvia: picking this up — oncall here. seeing the same on grafana, spike started ~08:12 UTC. p95 ~850ms, p99 ~2.6s, streaming stall count up x6.

Kai: thanks. Any single-tenant hotness?

Sylvia: initial breakdown: mixed-seqlen jobs up 30% on cont-batcher Q. KV-cache miss rate ticked up. Looks multi-tenant but a couple customers (cust-A, cust-C) show high seqlen variance in traces.

Raj: adding logs from one host (usw2-gpu-12):
```
[08:13:02] batcher: enqueue req id=abc123 len=2048
[08:13:03] batcher: pack size=48 estimated_tokens=1200
[08:13:03] scheduler: context switch preempt tenant=cust-A weight=1 -> delayed
[08:13:04] streaming: stall detected stream_id=stream-xyz reason=kv-fetch-latency
[08:13:06] batcher: send to runtime host=rt-45 latency_ms=2420
```

Marta: kv-store latency increased to ~300ms for some keys during spike. Could be transient K/V hotness causing downstream paging in runtime.

Sylvia: mitigation plan in order: 1) throttle cont-batcher max_pack_size to 32 for affected pool, 2) enable preemptive scheduling (fair share) for streaming-only queues, 3) force-retry KV hot keys (ttl bump), 4) if still bad, move heavy tenants to reserved queue. I'll run 1+2 now.

Kai: +1. Please post commands and confirm when done. I'll start customer-impact assessment and page CS.

Sylvia: running command:
```
# reduce max pack size on pool
redctl pools update --pool usw2-gpu --cont-batcher.max_pack_size 32 --reason "p99 spike"
# enable fairshare preemption
redctl scheduler set --pool usw2-gpu --fairshare.preemptive true
```

Sylvia: applied both on pool usw2-gpu. Changes pushed to 4/6 hosts, rolling restart for batcher needed on 2 hosts (in flight).

Raj: seeing pack sizes drop to 28-32 now, queue depth decreasing. p95 trending down to ~700ms after ~40s. p99 still ~1.4s (improved). streaming stalls reduced but not zero.

Marta: KV latency back to ~120ms after TTL bump for some hot keys. Not fully resolved. suspecting a small set of long-seq requests causing pack amplification + KV thrash.

Kai: customer-impact note for CS: preliminary — 2 customers (cust-A, cust-B) had >=10% requests exceed SLO in last 10m. No widespread error increase, just latency. Will update PD incident. @support-bot can you notify support channel for these tenants and attach dashboard?

support-bot: Notifying #support-high-touch: "PSA — potential latency for cust-A and cust-B. Link: https://dash.redwood.local/alerts/3170001111"

Sylvia: next step: isolate top offender traces. Raj, can you run trace filter on batcher logs for seqlen>1500 and top 20 tenants?

Raj: running query now. Result: cust-A (20% of large seq requests), cust-B (8%), cust-D (4%). The top offending handler is the reranker pipeline from cust-A — consistently packs with a few huge seqs + many small ones -> padding amplification.

Marta: idea: enable per-tenant cap on max_batch_fraction to prevent one tenant from inflating pack sizes. We can blacklist cust-A temporarily from cont-batching and route to dedicated small-batch runtime.

Sylvia: blacklisting min-impact first: move cust-A large seq traffic to the fallback small-batch route (no cont-batching). Command:
```
# route rule to bypass cont-batch for cust-A large-seq
redctl routing add --tenant cust-A --when "seq_len>1024" --route small-batch-runtime --ttl 30m --reason "live mitigation"
```

Sylvia: rule applied. Telemetry shows 95% of cust-A large seq now bypass cont-batcher.

Raj: p99 dropped to ~920ms after routing change. queue depth stabilized. streaming stalls nearly cleared. Looks like culprit was packing amplification from long sequences.

Kai: customer comms draft: "We observed elevated latency affecting a subset of requests for cust-A and cust-B. We have applied a temporary routing change for long-sequence requests to mitigate risk. We're monitoring and will follow up with RCA." Sending to CS for approval.

Marta: ops note — follow-up action items: 1) add automatic tenant-level pack caps and mitigation rules, 2) improve KV hotkey detection and pre-emptive eviction strategy, 3) add eval for mixed-seqlen workload to cont-batcher canary.

Sylvia: agree. Also propose a short-term scheduler tweak: reduce pack amplification window from 500ms -> 200ms to reduce latency amplification for mixed workloads.

Raj: quick check on client-visible error rates: 5xx not increased; some streaming timeouts down from 1.1% -> 0.7% during mitigation.

Kai: handoff to next oncall (luis) in 15m. @luis please monitor for 30m and escalate if p99 > 1s or streaming stall > 2/min.

Luis: oncall ack — I'll take it. Will watch dashboards and logs.

Sylvia: summary for incident: root cause — packing amplification from mixed long/short seqs in continuous-batching plus transient KV hotkey latency. Immediate mitigations: reduced pack size, enabled preemptive fairshare, applied tenant routing for long-seq bypass. Impact: p99 peaked ~2.6s, affected small subset of tenants (cust-A, cust-B), no increased error rates. Follow-ups assigned to infra/serving teams.

Kai: marking this incident as "live-mitigation resolved" for now. Creating PD incident and linking to thread. PD: INC-3170001111.

incident-bot: Incident INC-3170001111 created and assigned to eng-oncall. Severity: Sev2.

Marta: adding ticket for batcher improvements: https://issues.redwood.local/ISSUE-8921 (auto tenant caps + canary).

Sylvia: thanks team. Closing active mitigations; luis will monitor. If any regression or reoccurrence, reopen and escalate. :thumbsup:

Luis: noted. I'll post a short postmortem draft if stable after 24h.

support-bot: Notified customer success and attached the dashboard + comms draft.

Sylvia: end of thread.
